payload.claim: The spec's own notes require the `_deferred_finish_home` fixture to create a second, newer closed batch (budget 10.0, `BUDGET`, no layer) alongside the batch under test, specifically so the finish witness cannot pass by accident if the implementation reads 'the newest batch' instead of the batch named by `args.batch_id`. The actual fixture in `tests/test_cli.py` (`_deferred_finish_home`) creates only one batch, so every ledger lookup in `_finish` that is keyed on `args.batch_id` (starting with the `status_row` query at this line) is indistinguishable, in the test, from a lookup that simply grabs the most recent row. Replacing `"SELECT status FROM batches WHERE batch_id = ?", (args.batch_id,)` with `"SELECT status FROM batches ORDER BY batch_id DESC LIMIT 1"` (dropping the batch_id filter entirely) keeps both new witnesses green, because in every fixture instance there is exactly one batch row, yet it breaks the acceptance criterion that `finish <batch id>` reads that batch's own row rather than whichever batch happens to be newest.
